args.message:
Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN for banker's rounding per FIN-212

The docstring claimed banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212,
but the implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP, causing the nightly build's
tests/test_money.py to fail (e.g. 2.665 rounded to 2.67 instead of 2.66).

Fix: import and use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in round_money.

args.head: fix/money-half-even-rounding
args.title: Fix banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary

The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212) for `round_money`, but `src/money.py` implemented it with ROUND_HALF_UP despite its docstring claiming ROUND_HALF_EVEN. Examples affected: 2.665 rounded to 2.67 instead of 2.66.

## Changes

- `src/money.py`: import `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` and use it as the rounding mode in `round_money`'s `quantize` call.

## CI

CI run `ci-0001` passed on `08d3cd5986`.

Needed for today's release — requesting review from code-owner.

6. **Verified**: `src/money.py` on main now uses `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, so the nightly test expectation is satisfied and today's release includes the fix.
